findings.title: Line exceeds 88 chars; ruff E501 will fail lint
findings.description: The `except Exception as error:  # noqa: BLE001 - the Runner's one process boundary (D8)` line is over 88 characters. The grep confirmed it is the only over-length line in `src/amoeba/runner`. The baseline ruff config selects `E` and sets `line-length = 88`, so E501 should flag it, and `BLE001` is already suppressed on that line. Move the justification onto a separate comment line above the `except`, keeping a short `# noqa: BLE001` on the `except` line. I did not run `ruff check` to confirm the failure.

findings.title: Run-id and entry-parameter validation duplicated in three places
findings.description: `finish._run_id`, `observe.RunObserver._observe_one` and `launch._text_parameter` each check that the journal entry's run id (or other parameter) is a non-empty string. They raise `ValueError` with slightly different messages. `_observe_one` also accepts an empty string while `_run_id` in `finish.py` does not, so the same entry can pass one check and fail the other. Put one accessor next to `JournalEntry` or in `launch.py` and use it from all three places, as the DRY rule requires.

findings.title: Test reaches into private tenant state, and the single-`except` guard is brittle
findings.description: `test_the_runner_package_has_exactly_one_broad_except` counts the substring `except Exception` in source text. A comment or docstring containing that text would break it, and a different broad form such as `except BaseException` would not be counted. `test_factory.py` also reads `tenant._planners` and `test_tenant.py` reads `tenant._tracker`, both with pyright suppressions. Rely on the `BLE` ruff rule for the first, and on public behaviour for the second, instead of source-text or private-attribute checks.

findings.title: `LaunchTracker.confirm` raises `KeyError` for an untracked id
findings.description: Current callers only confirm entries they have just fetched via `get`, so I found no path to the error today. The method is public and silently differs from `forget`, which tolerates unknown ids. Document the precondition or make the two consistent.

findings.title: Fault ordering relies on store deduplication
findings.description: `raise_expected_faults` tracks `already_open` locally and also calls `raise_project_escalation` for every fault, relying on the store to deduplicate. That is fine if the store dedupes on `(project, kind)` as documented. I did not inspect the store, so this depends on that contract holding.
